change.title: pr-2-flat
change.description: Optimize spans buffer insertion with eviction during insert
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator uses numeric key handling on a datetime column
findings.body: `get_item_key` and `value_from_cursor` are copied from `Paginator`, which assumes a numeric key. The audit log endpoint orders by `-datetime`, so `getattr(item, self.key)` returns a `datetime`. `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError`. `build_cursor` calls the key function on the results, so every `optimized_pagination=true` request that returns rows fails with a 500. The `DateTimePaginator` that the endpoint uses today converts to `timestamp*multiplier` in `get_item_key` (paginator.py:233-236) and back to a datetime in `value_from_cursor` (paginator.py:238-241). This class does neither. On a second page, the cursor's integer value would also be compared raw against the `datetime` column in `build_queryset`. The class is also a near-verbatim copy of `BasePaginator.get_result` (about 70 lines) that differs only in the negative-offset branch. Subclassing `DateTimePaginator` and overriding only the slicing would avoid both problems.

findings.title: Negative-offset path cannot work; Django rejects negative slicing
findings.body: The comment says "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically", and this is false. `QuerySet.__getitem__` asserts on a negative start or stop ("Negative indexing is not supported."). `Cursor.from_string` accepts a negative offset from the request (`int(bits[1])`, cursors.py:59), so `?cursor=0:-5:0` together with `optimized_pagination=true` reaches `queryset[-5:...]` and returns a 500. If the slice did work, it would let the caller reach rows outside the cursor window. The justification "permissions are checked at the queryset level" only holds for the organization filter, not for pagination bounds. The advanced branch has no working behaviour and should be removed. If negative offsets are really wanted, validate the offset and implement it explicitly.

findings.title: Shared BasePaginator now silently clamps negative offsets, and the comment misdescribes it
findings.body: This edits `BasePaginator.get_result`, which every `Paginator` and `DateTimePaginator` endpoint uses. It does not enable negative offsets as the comment says. For a forward cursor, `max(0, offset)` now serves rows from 0 where it used to fail the Django negative-index assertion. `build_cursor` still derives the next and prev offsets from the unclamped `cursor.offset` (cursors.py:141). With a negative offset, the page contents and the returned next cursor disagree, so pages can repeat or skip. For `is_prev` cursors, `offset` is passed through unchanged and still fails. Nothing in the PR description or the spans change calls for this edit. Revert it, and validate offsets (reject negatives with a 400) in the cursor parser if hardening is wanted.

findings.title: `organization_context.member` can be None, and the check is evaluated on every request
findings.body: `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is `RpcOrganizationMember | None` (organizations/services/organization/model.py:346), and access.py guards against `None` in several places. `enable_advanced` is computed before the `use_optimized` check, so it runs on every audit-log request, not only the opt-in ones. For a non-superuser with no member row (for example token-based access), `.has_global_access` raises `AttributeError`. That breaks the default listing path. Compute the check lazily (`use_optimized and (...)`) and guard `member is None`.

findings.title: Unrelated audit-log feature in a spans-buffer PR; misleading comments and trailing whitespace
findings.body: The PR is described as "Optimize spans buffer insertion with eviction during insert", but this file, `OptimizedCursorPaginator` and the `Cursor` comments add an undocumented, admin-gated pagination mode to a public API. This should be a separate PR with its own tests. Comments such as "Performance optimization" and "high-performance audit log navigation" are not backed by any query change. Lines 72 and 89 also have trailing whitespace. No tests cover the new branch.

findings.title: Comment on `Cursor.offset` claims negative offsets are supported
findings.body: `self.offset = int(offset)` is unchanged, and no code path supports negative offsets (Django rejects them; see the paginator findings). The comment is false and invites misuse. Remove it.

findings.title: Redirect-chain limit lowered 10x without explanation, and the explanatory comment was removed
findings.body: The loop bound went from 10000 to 1000, and the comment saying that trees deeper than the bound may not be joined correctly was deleted. Nothing in the spans-eviction change needs this. Segment trees deeper than 1000 now fail to join, and the only trace is `redirect_depth` in the metrics gauge. If the lower bound is intentional, restore the comment and say why it was lowered.

findings.title: Silent eviction replaces a logged and metered segment skip; limit hard-coded and `max_segment_spans` now dead
findings.body: Previously, a segment over `max_segment_spans` was skipped in `_load_segment_data` with a metric (`segment_span_count_exceeded`) and an error log. Now `zpopmin` drops the oldest spans (lowest `end_timestamp_precise`) with no metric or log. The segment is flushed truncated and nobody can see it. The limit is hard-coded as 1000 in Lua, while `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` (buffer.py:150, default 1001) is still accepted and stored but no longer read anywhere. Return the evicted count from the script and emit a metric in `process_spans`. Pass the limit as an ARGV from `max_segment_spans`, or remove the parameter. Also, `zunionstore` defaults to `AGGREGATE SUM`, so a payload present in both merged sets gets summed scores. That distorts eviction order. Use `AGGREGATE MAX` or `MIN`.

findings.title: Set-to-zset key type change has no migration; in-flight keys will hit WRONGTYPE
findings.body: The same `span-buf:s:*` keys change from SET (`sadd`/`sscan`/`scard`) to ZSET (`zadd`/`zscan`/`zcard`). Segments buffered by the previous release still exist as SETs, with TTL up to `redis_ttl` (3600s). During or after deploy, `zcard`/`zunionstore` in the Lua script, `zadd`, or `zscan` on those keys return WRONGTYPE. A Lua error inside a pipelined EVALSHA fails `p.execute()` for the whole batch, which can crash-loop the consumer until the keys expire. Either roll out with a key-prefix or version bump, or drain the buffer before deploying.

findings.title: No test for the new eviction-on-insert behaviour
findings.body: The tests only add the new `end_timestamp_precise` argument to existing cases. Nothing covers the new behaviour: that a segment over 1000 spans is trimmed to 1000, that the oldest-by-timestamp spans are the ones evicted, that the root span survives, or that the zset merge keeps scores correct. Add a test that inserts more than 1000 spans with distinct timestamps and asserts what `flush_segments` returns. All tests also use one identical timestamp (1700000000.0), so score ordering is never exercised.

contracts.action: New `optimized_pagination=true` request path for audit logs using OptimizedCursorPaginator
contracts.before_after: The existing path converts datetime to a ms timestamp in get_item_key and back in value_from_cursor (paginator.py:233-241). The new class copies the numeric Paginator versions (paginator.py:838-843), so datetime keys fail in math.floor and cursor values are compared raw against a datetime column.
contracts.visible_effect: Admins (superuser or has_global_access) using the flag get a 500 whenever rows exist; non-flag users are unaffected, except non-member non-superusers, who hit a None dereference at line 71.
contracts.failure_mode: TypeError in get_item_key; AttributeError when member is None; AssertionError for negative offsets (Django negative indexing).

contracts.action: Spans buffer stores segments as Redis ZSETs and evicts to 1000 spans inside add-buffer.lua
contracts.equivalent_path: Old path: sadd, then sunionstore in Lua, then a span-count check at flush in _load_segment_data (skipped the whole segment with a metric and an error log)
contracts.before_after: Before: an oversized segment was dropped at flush, logged and metered. After: the oldest spans are popped at insert with no signal; the flush-time count check was removed (buffer.py:446-449).
contracts.visible_effect: Segments with more than 1000 spans are flushed truncated, and no one is notified.
contracts.failure_mode: Existing SET keys at deploy time cause WRONGTYPE errors in the script and in zscan; the error propagates from the pipeline execute.

summary: The spans-buffer change (SET to ZSET with eviction in Lua) is mostly coherent, but it evicts spans silently and leaves `max_segment_spans` unused. It also lowers the redirect-depth limit without a reason and has no migration for existing SET keys. The audit-log `OptimizedCursorPaginator` is unrelated to the PR description. As written it returns a 500 on any non-empty result, because the numeric key handling is applied to a datetime column. Its negative-offset path is rejected by Django, and the member check can dereference `None`. The edit to the shared `BasePaginator` silently changes how every paginator treats negative offsets. Tests only add the new argument and do not cover eviction.
